- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent high), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently fails to recover → add 2–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment > 0.1 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in downward trends → if 3+ consecutive days of falling prices, forecast should be 1–2% above recent low to avoid premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) → apply 3–5% downward adjustment to first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more) in last 5 days, model exhibits high variance → use 20-day EWMA of true values as smoothing anchor for forecast adjustment.
